text: What is most underrated problem in fast-moving teams? 👇🏼 It's 'Tribal knowledge' — all the critical unwritten knowledge the team depends on, but no one writes down. This is more common than you think. Engineering and data teams build up a lot of “unwritten” knowledge — architecture decisions, modeling trade-offs, data nuances — but much of it stays undocumented. It lives across Slack threads, Gmail, Notion, JIRA, calendar invites — and in people’s heads. When you have high turnover, that knowledge doesn’t transfer — and new team members are left without critical context. And this isn’t limited to small team; it happens in big tech too: 💡 Why certain architectural choices were made 📊 What data pipelines are deprecated (and why) 🗂️ Metrics definitions that have evolved — with no clear paper trail And I’ve seen the exact same dynamic play out in my own small business too. As a content creator, I run a small part-time team — many of them do this as a side hustle. People come and go. And every time someone new joins, onboarding takes weeks — because so much of what we do isn’t documented, it lives in past threads and my inbox. I’ve been testing @TankaAI (https://lnkd.in/gP4XWcKY) to solve this. hashtag #ad It integrates across Slack, Gmail, Notion, Calendar, ChatGPT — and builds a living, searchable “team brain”, which converts scattered information into structured files for retention and sharing.
